title: Part 9: A Psycho-History of American Psychology - It's What You (Don't) See

sentences.en: My hands on the humming lap, like it's some old buried stone.
sentences.zh: 我的双手放在嗡嗡作响的膝盖上，仿佛那是某种埋藏已久的古老石头。

sentences.en: I ask it the oldest questions, it answers and I look to no slow by these broken roads.
sentences.zh: 我向它提出最古老的问题，它回答我，而我在这条崎岖的道路上不再感到迟疑。

sentences.en: Hey guys, it's Joel, and welcome back to Psychotherapy on the Couch, the psychohistory of American psychology.
sentences.zh: 嘿，大家好，我是乔尔，欢迎回到《沙发上的心理治疗》，这是一档关于美国心理学心理史的节目。

sentences.en: What psychology can see, what it can't see, and why it has trouble telling the difference.
sentences.zh: 探讨心理学能看到什么，不能看到什么，以及为什么它难以区分这两者。

sentences.en: Until now.
sentences.zh: 直到现在。

sentences.en: This is part nine, the end, the last one.
sentences.zh: 这是第九部分，也是终章，最后一集。

sentences.en: Thank you for bearing with me.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家的耐心陪伴。

sentences.en: So eight episodes of describing how the apparatus got built, why we call it what we call it,
sentences.zh: 前八集我们描述了这套机制是如何建立的，为什么我们这样称呼它，

sentences.en: why we can't see it, and why it has done the practice of sitting with another human being, I think, a disservice.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们看不透它，以及我认为，它为何辜负了与另一个人坐在一起进行治疗的初衷。

sentences.en: Which is not that hard.
sentences.zh: 这其实并不难。

sentences.en: It's one of the easier things to do, at least for me.
sentences.zh: 至少对我来说，这是最容易做到的事情之一。

sentences.en: In the last episode, I tried to lay out where the science of the future is pointing, what the science of the past has already told us multiple times,
sentences.zh: 在上一集中，我试图阐述未来科学的指向，以及过去科学已经多次告诉我们的事实，

sentences.en: and which information, you know, the clinician as instrument catches as we approach the frontier, because the frontier moves too fast for any manual to capture.
sentences.zh: 还有当我们在接近前沿时，作为“工具”的临床医生捕捉到了哪些信息，因为前沿移动得太快，任何手册都无法将其囊括。

sentences.en: Psychology itself may be changing faster than any other point in history.
sentences.zh: 心理学本身的变化速度可能比历史上任何时期都要快。

sentences.en: You look at something like Moore's law that says computing power is going to get faster.
sentences.zh: 看看摩尔定律，它说计算能力会越来越快。

sentences.en: Well, you look at my thesis and other people's thesis from anthropology that we draw different metaphors about the self
sentences.zh: 你看，我的论文以及其他人关于人类学的论文都指出，我们对自我、

sentences.en: and psychology and psychopathology and what we are, what we're supposed to be, how we make meaning from technology.
sentences.zh: 心理学、精神病理学，以及我们是什么、我们应该成为什么、我们如何从技术中赋予意义，有着不同的隐喻。

sentences.en: Well, Moore's law says that it's going to double in speed and increase exponentially.
sentences.zh: 摩尔定律说，速度会翻倍并呈指数级增长。

sentences.en: From there, then what does that say about how psychology will change?
sentences.zh: 那么，这对于心理学将如何改变意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: But hell, maybe I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 但见鬼，也许我错了。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: And then I guess that question would not be relevant to the future.
sentences.zh: 我想那个问题对未来来说可能并不重要。

sentences.en: So how does the field produce a generation of clinicians who can see what is wrong,
sentences.zh: 那么，该领域如何培养出一代能够看清问题所在的临床医生，

sentences.en: who can see and name what is wrong, who have the evidence base, real evidence to say what is wrong and then change it?
sentences.zh: 能够看清并指出问题所在，拥有循证基础，有真正的证据来说明问题并加以改变？

sentences.en: Well, that's the question this episode is about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是本集要探讨的问题。

sentences.en: So one thing that we should look at is reverence and the other is complexity.
sentences.zh: 我们应该关注的一点是“敬畏”，另一点是“复杂性”。

sentences.en: You know, together they form this effective institutional defense system, you know, an egoic type defense, but not an individual in a macro, in a, in an American professional life.
sentences.zh: 它们共同构成了一种有效的制度防御系统，一种自我防御，但不是针对个人，而是在宏观层面，在某种美国职业生活中。

sentences.en: Um, you know, you can't fix psychiatry or psychology or social work or counseling or any of the free licensed mental health professions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你无法修复精神病学、心理学、社会工作、咨询或任何持证心理健康专业。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: until you understand how reverence and complexity work together to keep the field unaccountable to the people it claims to serve and to the practitioners it claims to enforce accountability upon.
sentences.zh: 除非你理解敬畏和复杂性是如何共同作用，使该领域对其声称服务的人群以及其声称要强制问责的从业者免于问责的。

sentences.en: And what I want to put down is, you know, walk through the structural pieces.
sentences.zh: 我想做的是，梳理一下这些结构性的部分。

sentences.en: We already did some of that.
sentences.zh: 我们之前已经做过一些了。

sentences.en: Um, but it's not that the apparatus is captured.
sentences.zh: 但并不是说这套机制被“俘获”了。

sentences.en: The apparatus was constituted from its, in its very beginning, a defense against the mystery of psychological work.
sentences.zh: 这套机制从一开始就是为了防御心理工作的神秘性而建立的。

sentences.en: And it was made that way, not by the smartest people, not by the best people, not even really by the most influential people, but from the most useful people to it.
sentences.zh: 它之所以被这样制造出来，不是因为最聪明的人，不是因为最好的人，甚至不是因为最有影响力的人，而是因为对它最有用的人。

sentences.en: The ones who could not tolerate the mystery and needed to convert the work into something that could be procedurally administered.
sentences.zh: 那些无法忍受神秘感，需要将工作转化为可以按程序管理的人。

sentences.en: They're not really ever the beSt.
sentences.zh: 他们从来都不是最优秀的。

sentences.en: Just go through the most interesting people in the series or the most interesting people in history.
sentences.zh: 只要看看这个系列中最有趣的人，或者历史上最有趣的人就知道了。

sentences.en: It's not the winners that win.
sentences.zh: 赢家并不总是获胜者。

sentences.en: And that is a thesis that I will lightly put down.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我将轻描淡写提出的论点。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, the reference and the complexity that hold the apparatus in place are not just sociological armor in a generic sense.
sentences.zh: 但是，支撑这套机制的敬畏和复杂性，不仅仅是广义上的社会学盔甲。

sentences.en: They are institutional expression of a specific psychological problem.
sentences.zh: 它们是一个特定心理问题的制度化表达。

sentences.en: You know, the people who built and run the apparatus need psychology to be the kind of thing that it is not.
sentences.zh: 那些建立并运行这套机制的人，需要心理学成为它本不属于的那种东西。

sentences.en: And they've spent a hundred years rebuilding the field and the image of what they needed it to be.
sentences.zh: 他们花了一百年时间，按照他们所需要的样子重建了这个领域。

sentences.en: Largely because they needed you to be different than I think you are.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是因为他们需要你变得与我认为的你不同。

sentences.en: And the metrics, the manuals, the protocols, the credentialing, the licensure, the evidence base,
sentences.zh: 而那些指标、手册、协议、认证、执照、循证基础，

sentences.en: the entire infrastructure is the externalized form of an internal incapacity on their part.
sentences.zh: 整个基础设施都是他们内在无能的外化形式。

sentences.en: And it is the failure to tolerate mystery scaled into institutional architecture.
sentences.zh: 这是无法容忍神秘感而将其规模化为制度架构的失败。

sentences.en: I'm not even making, you know, big go out and do something.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不是在说要你们出去做什么大事。

sentences.en: A lot of these people are dead, right?
sentences.zh: 这些人很多都已经死了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, a hundred years old.
sentences.zh: 我是说，一百年了。

sentences.en: We basically started with the Indians with the series.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上是从这个系列的印第安人开始讲起的。

sentences.en: I'm just asking you to notice patterns in history.
sentences.zh: 我只是请你注意历史中的模式。

sentences.en: And in that we might notice how to make fail safes against the psychology of history and the history of psychology to make a better future.
sentences.zh: 从中我们或许能注意到如何针对历史的心理学和心理学的历史建立故障保险，以创造一个更好的未来。

sentences.en: But I don't think any of these things go away.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这些东西都不会消失。

sentences.en: No matter what kind of bureaucracy you build, I think you're always going to be noticing human nature and trying to anticipate its worst parts.
sentences.zh: 无论你建立什么样的官僚机构，我认为你总会注意到人性，并试图预判其最糟糕的部分。

sentences.en: And when you stop doing that, that's when they won.
sentences.zh: 当你停止这样做时，他们就赢了。

sentences.en: And I remember learning about the Holocaust in, like, ninth grade or something.
sentences.zh: 我记得在九年级左右学过大屠杀。

sentences.en: And they were saying, like, people did this bad thing for no reason.
sentences.zh: 当时他们说，人们无缘无故地做了这件坏事。

sentences.en: And they were just really bad.
sentences.zh: 他们只是真的很坏。

sentences.en: And then after they were done doing it, it's important that we talk about it so that we make sure that, you know, we know that they did this thing.
sentences.zh: 在他们做完之后，我们谈论它很重要，这样我们就能确保，你知道，我们知道他们做了这件事。

sentences.en: And that was just kind of the attitude of the teacher in the class.
sentences.zh: 这就是课堂上老师的态度。

sentences.en: And I was like, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，等一下。

sentences.en: No, I think, like, this is the baseline of what when we slip, we fall onto.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为，这正是我们滑倒时会跌落的基准线。

sentences.en: And we do that over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我们一次又一次地这样做。

sentences.en: And so we should be making sure that it doesn't happen again and actively trying to prevent it,
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该确保它不再发生，并积极尝试预防它，

sentences.en: not just holding it up as a monument for a bad thing that happened that can never happen again.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅把它作为一个纪念碑，纪念一件发生过且永远不会再发生的坏事。

sentences.en: And they were like, yeah, yeah, we should prevent it.
sentences.zh: 他们说，是的，是的，我们应该预防它。

sentences.en: But, you know, the point is this is like the worst thing ever and nothing will ever be that bad.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，这是有史以来最糟糕的事情，没有什么会比这更糟糕了。

sentences.en: I was like, well, let's go further back.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，让我们追溯得更远一点。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一件坏事。

sentences.en: But, like, doesn't this just seem like the thing that we do that when we stop being able to see it, when we dissociate from our capacity to do it, we are doing it.
sentences.zh: 但难道这看起来不像我们一直在做的事情吗？当我们无法看清它，当我们与自己做这件事的能力解离时，我们其实正在做它。

sentences.en: Or we are not far away from doing it.
sentences.zh: 或者我们离做这件事并不遥远。

sentences.en: And I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: They disagreed with me.
sentences.zh: 他们不同意我的观点。

sentences.en: Then maybe you disagree with me now.
sentences.zh: 也许你现在也不同意我。

sentences.en: But leave that on the table.
sentences.zh: 但先把这个问题放在一边。

sentences.en: Because if you walk into this episode thinking that the problem is bureaucratic drift or capture, you do miss a point that maybe I didn't make very well.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你带着“问题是官僚主义漂移或被俘获”的想法进入这一集，你可能就错过了一个我没讲清楚的重点。

sentences.en: You know, bureaucratic drift can be reformed by better policy.
sentences.zh: 官僚主义漂移可以通过更好的政策来改革。

sentences.en: But what we have here is something else.
sentences.zh: 但我们这里的情况是另一回事。

sentences.en: It's a field whose practitioners in disproportionate numbers entered the work because they could not tolerate the mystery the work is fundamentally constituted by, I think,
sentences.zh: 这是一个领域，其从业者中有很大一部分进入这个行业是因为他们无法忍受这项工作本质上所包含的神秘感，我认为，

sentences.en: and who have built and maintained an institutional structure that allows them to continue working in the field without ever having to solve, not the mystery,
sentences.zh: 他们建立并维护了一个制度结构，使他们能够继续在该领域工作，而无需解决——不是神秘感本身，

sentences.en: but the encounter with the mystery.
sentences.zh: 而是与神秘感的邂逅。

sentences.en: And, man, psychologists getting in a fight about this thing, I think,
sentences.zh: 天哪，我认为心理学家们为此争吵，

sentences.en: is an indication of the field doing well when they're all accusing each other of not sitting with the mystery enough or not having, you know, a deep enough, like, who is it?
sentences.zh: 反而说明这个领域做得还不错，当他们互相指责对方没有足够地与神秘感共处，或者没有，你知道，足够深刻的，比如，那是谁？

sentences.en: Oh, crap.
sentences.zh: 该死。

sentences.en: What's his name?
sentences.zh: 他叫什么名字？

sentences.en: The guy who's, like, almost Carl Jung, but it's backwards.
sentences.zh: 那个几乎是卡尔·荣格，但却是反过来的家伙。

sentences.en: Psychosynthesis.
sentences.zh: 意象综合疗法。

sentences.en: Who is the psychosynthesis guy?
sentences.zh: 意象综合疗法的那个人是谁？

sentences.en: Roberto Asageli.
sentences.zh: 罗伯托·阿萨吉奥利。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 对了，就是他。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's, like, almost Carl Jung except backwards.
sentences.zh: 是的，他几乎就是卡尔·荣格，只是反过来的。

sentences.en: Because Jung is, like, you should analyze the darkness in order to understand it and then fill it up with the light of awareness.
sentences.zh: 因为荣格是说，你应该分析黑暗以理解它，然后用觉知的亮光填满它。

sentences.en: And then he's, like, no, you just go into the light of awareness and then it will burn away the darkness.
sentences.zh: 而他是说，不，你直接进入觉知的亮光，它就会烧掉黑暗。

sentences.en: And they, like, kind of make an opposite model.
sentences.zh: 他们算是建立了一个相反的模型。

sentences.en: But then they judge each other.
sentences.zh: 但他们互相评判。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're both, like, he is not as deep and spiritual as I am because I'm going deeper.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们都觉得，他没有我深刻，没有我精神，因为我钻得更深。

sentences.en: I'm being more spiritual.
sentences.zh: 我更具灵性。

sentences.en: And, like, yeah, you know, psychologists fighting in this way 100 years ago is kind of insufferable as it is today.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，心理学家一百年前这样争吵，和今天一样令人难以忍受。

sentences.en: But I do think that it is a symptom of a healthy field because, you know, we're all students in this thing.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为这是领域健康的一种症状，因为，你知道，我们都是这个领域里的学生。

sentences.en: And when you see, you know, people who are kind of being insufferable in that way in an English department their freshman year or philosophy department or, you know, one of those,
sentences.zh: 当你看到，你知道，那些在大一英语系或哲学系里表现得令人难以忍受的人，或者，你知道，类似的情况，

sentences.en: that attitude.
sentences.zh: 那种态度。

sentences.en: It's not that they're right.
sentences.zh: 并不是他们是对的。

sentences.en: It's that they are after something that we've loSt.
sentences.zh: 而是他们在追求某种我们已经丢失的东西。

sentences.en: And I kind of miss, you know, those fights.
sentences.zh: 我有点怀念那些争论。

sentences.en: So, you know, the bureaucracy is the symptom.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，官僚主义只是症状。

sentences.en: And it is the hungry ghost obsession with the mechanism of action.
sentences.zh: 这是对作用机制的“饿鬼”般的执念。

sentences.en: And we have to figure out why it is that the change happens, you know, as this mechanistic variable.
sentences.zh: 我们必须弄清楚为什么变化会发生，你知道，作为这种机械论的变量。

sentences.en: And the reverence and the complexity are the symptom.
sentences.zh: 敬畏和复杂性是症状。

sentences.en: And the actual disease is that the people who should be most comfortable with what cannot be measured are, by selection and by training, the people least comfortable with it.
sentences.zh: 真正的疾病在于，那些本应最能适应不可测量事物的人，通过筛选和训练，反而成了最不适应它的人。

sentences.en: And they have used their institutional power to make the field unable to admit the unmeasurable.
sentences.zh: 他们利用自己的制度权力，使该领域无法承认不可测量的事物。

sentences.en: And that is where the work will always happen.
sentences.zh: 而那正是工作永远会发生的地方。

sentences.en: And I want to start with something that's been on my mind throughout the whole series.
sentences.zh: 我想从我整个系列中一直思考的一件事开始。

sentences.en: I guess end with something, which is that the question of, like, when that capture happened.
sentences.zh: 我想以一件事结束，那就是关于这种俘获何时发生的问题。

sentences.en: Because the way that I've been describing it in the previous episodes,
sentences.zh: 因为我在前几集中描述它的方式，

sentences.en: you might come away thinking that a capture happens to clinicians after they're licensed or after they join an insurance panel, which, in my opinion,
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为俘获发生在临床医生获得执照或加入保险小组之后，在我看来，

sentences.en: really doesn't affect much other than, you know, the responsibilities that come with that.
sentences.zh: 这除了随之而来的责任外，并没有太大影响。

sentences.en: But they don't change that many things.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有改变太多事情。

sentences.en: You know, or the employers or the regulatory bodies hit with them and pressure them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，或者雇主或监管机构打击他们并向他们施压。

sentences.en: You know, this is an active control.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种主动控制。

sentences.en: And, I mean, there are institutional rules.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，确实有制度规则。

sentences.en: Some of them I agree with.
sentences.zh: 有些我同意。

sentences.en: Some of them I don't.
sentences.zh: 有些我不同意。

sentences.en: But that's a tiny part of it.
sentences.zh: 但这只是其中很小的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, it is not where the capture really starts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这并不是俘获真正开始的地方。

sentences.en: The capture starts earlier.
sentences.zh: 俘获开始得更早。

sentences.en: It starts in training.
sentences.zh: 它始于训练。

sentences.en: It starts in the way that the whole thing is framed to somebody who's walking in that is unfamiliar with any of it.
sentences.zh: 它始于整个框架对一个刚入门、对这一切都不熟悉的人的设定方式。

sentences.en: And the capture starts when a young doctor or social worker or psychologist is learning day by day what kinds of explanations they're going to be rewarded for offering.
sentences.zh: 俘获始于年轻的医生、社会工作者或心理学家日复一日地学习他们提供什么样的解释会得到奖励。

sentences.en: And what kinds of explanations they're going to be punished for offering.
sentences.zh: 以及提供什么样的解释会受到惩罚。

sentences.en: And the capture happens in graduate school.
sentences.zh: 俘获发生在研究生院。

sentences.en: The capture happens in residency.
sentences.zh: 俘获发生在住院医师实习期。

sentences.en: And by the time the licensed clinician walks into their first job, the capture is already done.
sentences.zh: 当持证临床医生走进他们的第一份工作时，俘获已经完成了。

sentences.en: You are serious if you are this way.
sentences.zh: 如果你是这样的人，你就是认真的。

sentences.en: And if you are not this way, you are not serious.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是这样的人，你就不是认真的。

sentences.en: Lucky for me, I thrive on not being taken seriously.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我不被认真对待反而活得更好。

sentences.en: I'm 100% trickster archetype.
sentences.zh: 我是百分之百的“捣蛋鬼”原型。

sentences.en: Whenever I detect somebody taking me slightly seriously, I make it as hard for them as possible until it becomes impossible.
sentences.zh: 每当我发现有人稍微认真对待我时，我就会尽可能让他们感到困难，直到变得不可能。

sentences.en: That may be part of the way that we have to have a passive resistance to a form of passive control.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我们必须对某种被动控制进行消极抵抗的方式的一部分。

sentences.en: Because I don't think that this is active control, and I don't think that there is an active resistance to it that is effective.
sentences.zh: 因为我不认为这是主动控制，我也不认为存在一种有效的主动抵抗。

sentences.en: I think it's going to be something that looks and sounds kind of like that.
sentences.zh: 我认为它将是某种看起来和听起来像那样的东西。

sentences.en: Tanya Lerman, you know, we talked about last time as the cultural anthropologist from Stanford.
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅·勒曼，你知道，我们上次谈到她是斯坦福大学的文化人类学家。

sentences.en: We talked about her watching the hearing voices in people with psychosis being different in first and third world countries.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到她观察到精神病患者在第一世界和第三世界国家听到的声音是不同的。

sentences.en: Well, you know, she did another thing that I like, wrote another book that I like.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，她还做了另一件我喜欢的事，写了另一本我喜欢的书。

sentences.en: Her book is Of Two Minds.
sentences.zh: 她的书是《两种思想》。

sentences.en: And it's interesting because it's documenting history that I think American psychiatric establishment, psychology establishment, wanted to ignore and largely did.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为它记录的历史我认为美国精神病学界、心理学界想要忽略，并且在很大程度上确实忽略了。

sentences.en: Even though it's sort of a study of kind of like what I'm doing here.
sentences.zh: 尽管它某种程度上是对我在这里所做的事情的研究。

sentences.en: It's a study of the psychology of the psychologist by an anthropologiSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一位人类学家对心理学家心理的研究。

sentences.en: So, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，

sentences.en: she looked at American psychiatric residents that were arriving at their training programs as young people who are interested in human suffering and how they changed at a specific time in history.
sentences.zh: 她观察了那些刚进入培训项目的美国精神科住院医师，他们原本是怀着对人类苦难的关切投身于此的年轻人，并记录了他们在特定历史时期所发生的变化。

sentences.en: And so many of them, you know, have been drawn to psychiatry because they wanted to understand minds and help people.
sentences.zh: 他们中许多人之所以被精神病学吸引，是因为他们想了解人类的思想并帮助他人。

sentences.en: And they arrive with this mix of curiosity.
sentences.zh: 他们带着这种混合的好奇心而来。

sentences.en: And some are interested in the psychological and some are interested in the biological.
sentences.zh: 有些人对心理学感兴趣，有些人则对生物学感兴趣。

sentences.en: And most are interested in both.
sentences.zh: 而大多数人对两者都感兴趣。

sentences.en: And how do they intersect?
sentences.zh: 那么它们是如何交织在一起的呢？

sentences.en: Where does the meat meet the soul?
sentences.zh: 肉体与灵魂在何处交汇？

sentences.en: And they imagine when they are entering training that they will learn to think across both registers and they'll become doctors who can hold a patient's biology and biography at the same time.
sentences.zh: 他们在开始培训时设想，自己将学会跨越这两个领域进行思考，成为既能关注患者生理状况又能理解其人生经历的医生。

sentences.en: And what happens to them over the four years of residency is that they're forced to, and this is the cohort she's following.
sentences.zh: 但在四年的住院医师培训中，他们被迫改变了，这就是她所追踪的群体。

sentences.en: I'm not saying that this is my opinion that it's happening to doctors.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这是我个人认为医生们正在经历的事情。

sentences.en: I'm telling you about the book.
sentences.zh: 我是在向你们介绍这本书的内容。

sentences.en: But the choice is not made.
sentences.zh: 但这种选择并非主动做出。

sentences.en: And thank you, Jason, for telling me about this book because I did not know about this one.
sentences.zh: 感谢你，Jason，告诉我这本书，因为我之前并不知道它。

sentences.en: And I appreciate you for that.
sentences.zh: 我很感激你。

sentences.en: So there is no moment where a senior faculty member sits down and the resident says, hey, you have to pick a side.
sentences.zh: 培训中并没有某个时刻，会有资深教员坐下来对住院医师说：嘿，你必须选边站。

sentences.en: They just sort of see these sides emerge.
sentences.zh: 他们只是看着这些立场逐渐显现。

sentences.en: You know, the choice is made by the structure of the training itself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种选择是由培训本身的结构决定的。

sentences.en: The reward selects through systemic selection, through where it gives rewards.
sentences.zh: 奖励机制通过系统性的筛选，决定了资源投向何处。

sentences.en: And she's following psychiatrists.
sentences.zh: 她追踪的是精神科医生。

sentences.en: I believe she starts in 89, but it's largely associated with changes that happened over the course of the 90s.
sentences.zh: 我相信她是从89年开始的，但这主要与90年代发生的变化有关。

sentences.en: And, you know, she's noticing that rewards are more important than punishments.
sentences.zh: 而且，她注意到奖励比惩罚更重要。

sentences.en: And I'm reminded of where Sidra Stone in, what is it, Embracing Ourselves, the Voice Dialogue Manual, where him and his wife, Sidra, because they co-wrote it, two authors,
sentences.zh: 这让我想起Sidra Stone在《拥抱我们自己：语音对话手册》中所写的，他和他的妻子Sidra，因为他们是合著者，两位作者，

sentences.en: I don't want to leave one out, said, the people who give us praise judge us much more strong than the people who give us punishment.
sentences.zh: 我不想漏掉任何一位，他们说，给予我们赞美的人对我们的评判，远比给予我们惩罚的人要强烈得多。

sentences.en: But she notices then, and she says, by the time the licensed clinician walks into their first job, that capture is already finished.
sentences.zh: 但她随后注意到，当获得执照的临床医生开始第一份工作时，这种“俘获”已经完成了。

sentences.en: But what capture?
sentences.zh: 但什么是“俘获”呢？

sentences.en: Psychiatric residency, you know, is organized around rotations, exams, case presentations, and they systematically privilege, she says, one kind of explanation over the other,
sentences.zh: 精神科住院医师培训围绕着轮转、考试和病例陈述展开，她说，这些培训系统性地偏袒某种解释，而排斥另一种，

sentences.en: depending on the one you get to.
sentences.zh: 取决于你接触到的是哪一种。

sentences.en: The biological explanations are the ones that get rewarded.
sentences.zh: 生物学解释是那些能获得奖励的。

sentences.en: The psychological explanations get tolerated sometimes, but they're increasingly framed as soft, as unscientific, as sort of a sport that you do when the real work is done,
sentences.zh: 心理学解释有时会被容忍，但它们越来越多地被贴上“软科学”、“不科学”的标签，被视为一种在正事做完后才进行的消遣，

sentences.en: or a sport that you watch when the real world, when the real work of medication is done.
sentences.zh: 或者是在药物治疗这项“真正的工作”完成后，才去关注的消遣。

sentences.en: You know, as the sort of thing that a resident might do on the side, once they've mastered the real work of medication management and DSM diagnosis to understand it.
sentences.zh: 就像是住院医师在掌握了药物管理和DSM诊断这些“正事”之后，顺手做做的事情。

sentences.en: And I definitely saw that when I was in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我在医院时确实看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Um, I think I got shut down almost every time I said anything in a ground rounds to a psychiatrist and we were supposed to talk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想每次我在大查房时对精神科医生说些什么，或者我们本该讨论时，我几乎每次都被打断。

sentences.en: But when I would talk, I mean, they would kind of literally roll their eyes and wave their hand because I would say like things like,
sentences.zh: 每当我开口，他们就会翻白眼、挥挥手，因为我会说类似这样的话：

sentences.en: I remember one time the guy said that patients report liking this and it's fine to do it because it stops them from coming back to the hospital as a psychotherapy technique.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次，那个人说患者报告喜欢这种心理治疗技术，而且这样做没问题，因为它能阻止患者再次入院。

sentences.en: Um, but it doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但它其实没用。

sentences.en: We know the evidence says it doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 我们知道证据显示它没用。

sentences.en: And I raised my hand and I was like, wait, so the patients report the symptom one way and they like it, but they, and they don't come back to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我举手说：等等，既然患者报告症状有所缓解，他们也喜欢，而且他们不再回医院了，

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: It doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 它没用？

sentences.en: And he said, well, you know, they've tested it and there's no mechanism of action there.
sentences.zh: 他说：嗯，你知道，他们测试过了，这背后没有作用机制。

sentences.en: And I was like, you mean they don't know what the mechanism of action is, but every time people do it, they get better.
sentences.zh: 我说：你的意思是他们不知道作用机制是什么，但每次人们这样做，他们都会好转。

sentences.en: They don't have symptoms and they don't come back to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 他们没有症状了，也不再回医院了。

sentences.en: And he just kind of said, yeah, you could do that as well as you could do anything else.
sentences.zh: 他只是说：嗯，你可以做那个，就像你可以做任何其他事情一样。

sentences.en: And I wanted to raise my hand again and say, Hey, but you mean, if you did something else though, then that wouldn't work.
sentences.zh: 我想再次举手说：嘿，但你的意思是，如果你做了别的事，那反而没用了？

sentences.en: You're talking about one thing that we know does, but like, anyway, uh, I wasn't that confident or antagonistic at that time.
sentences.zh: 你谈论的是一件我们知道有效的事情，但无论如何，嗯，我当时没那么自信或具有对抗性。

sentences.en: But, you know, Lerman says that there's a subtle pressure once you look for it in the same way that that statement that I repeated doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 但是，Lerman说，一旦你开始留意，就会发现一种微妙的压力，就像我刚才重复的那段话一样，逻辑上根本讲不通。

sentences.en: Um, you know, he was tracking one thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，他在追踪一件事。

sentences.en: This guy said out loud and the guy I asked was tracking one thing.
sentences.zh: 那个人大声说出来，而我问的那个人也在追踪一件事。

sentences.en: I know that this works based on my huge experience being a psychiatrist for a long time and seeing it done, that it has an effect, but the science tells me it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 我知道基于我作为精神科医生多年的丰富经验，看到它被实施，它确实有效，但科学告诉我它无效。

sentences.en: So I still have to kind of shame it as not being valid.
sentences.zh: 所以我还是得把它贬低为无效的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Um, you, I mean, you're, you're just saying out loud, the science disagrees with my experience, except I will dis, I will side against my experience because I have dissociated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你，我的意思是，你只是大声说出来，科学与我的经验相左，但我会选择反对我的经验，因为我已经解离了。

sentences.en: That's, that's strange, man.
sentences.zh: 这太奇怪了，伙计。

sentences.en: Um, so, you know, Lerman says, you know, these attendings, a lot of times they'll ask, you know, helpfully what medication are you considering?
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，Lerman说，这些主治医生，很多时候会很“热心”地问：你考虑用什么药物？

sentences.en: And then the resident learns every single time they bring up patient's family of, uh,
sentences.zh: 然后住院医师每次提到患者的家庭、

sentences.en: origin or history of trauma or the patient's attachment patterns or the patient's symbolic relationships or the way they connect with the patient or the way that, you know,
sentences.zh: 出身、创伤史、依恋模式、象征性关系、与患者的连接方式，或者他们如何，你知道，

sentences.en: they self-disclose their own suffering and they watch the patient improve.
sentences.zh: 自我披露自己的痛苦，并看着患者好转时，都会学到教训。

sentences.en: The person will be gently pushed back to medication, not saying medication doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 那个人会被温和地推回药物治疗，我不是说药物没用。

sentences.en: Just, she's noticing that,
sentences.zh: 只是，她注意到，

sentences.en: that they're not no longer interested in these other things in the hospital because the nineties represented a time where psychiatry was being forced to become a procedure, um,
sentences.zh: 他们在医院里不再对这些其他事情感兴趣，因为90年代是一个精神病学被迫转变为一种“程序”的时期，嗯，

sentences.en: instead of a process because we build based on procedures and everyone else could do procedures faster.
sentences.zh: 而不是一个“过程”，因为我们是按程序收费的，而其他人可以更快地完成程序。

sentences.en: And so it was already losing all this money and they were under all this, um, pressure to keep these, uh, psychiatry wings, um, basically in the,
sentences.zh: 所以它已经在亏钱了，他们承受着巨大的压力，要让这些精神科病房，嗯，基本上保持在，

sentences.en: as close to being in the black as they could, um, to keep them open.
sentences.zh: 尽可能实现收支平衡，嗯，以维持运营。

sentences.en: The managers are going to do that.
sentences.zh: 管理者们会这么做的。

sentences.en: So over time, the resident learned to present the case, the way that the attending wanted to hear it.
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，住院医师学会了以主治医生想听的方式来陈述病例。

sentences.en: And you know, the thing that I did not learn, this is what the doctors that had, you know, granted, uh,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我没学到的东西，这就是那些，你知道，背负着，嗯，

sentences.en: hundreds of thousands of dollars slunk in an education that they had to pay back.
sentences.zh: 数十万美元教育贷款的医生们所经历的。

sentences.en: So they learned symptom checklists.
sentences.zh: 所以他们学会了症状清单。

sentences.en: They learned DSM differentials.
sentences.zh: 他们学会了DSM鉴别诊断。

sentences.en: They learned medication responses.
sentences.zh: 他们学会了药物反应。

sentences.en: The biographical material just gets dropped.
sentences.zh: 个人经历的素材就这样被抛弃了。

sentences.en: And it's not because the resident has decided that the biographical material doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为住院医师认为个人经历的素材不重要。

sentences.en: It's because the resident has learned that the biographical material does not get rewarded and rewards are how training works.
sentences.zh: 而是因为住院医师已经学到，个人经历的素材得不到奖励，而奖励正是培训运作的方式。

sentences.en: I mean, very few times do you get punished in psychology training.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在心理学培训中，你很少受到惩罚。

sentences.en: If you're getting punished, you are maybe not going to be working for a while or ever again.
sentences.zh: 如果你受到惩罚，你可能就没法继续工作了，或者永远无法再从事这一行。

sentences.en: Um, so by the end of residency, Lerman says the residents have been formed into a particular kind of doctor and they can still talk about psychological material.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以到住院医师培训结束时，Lerman说，住院医师已经被塑造成了一种特定类型的医生，他们仍然可以谈论心理学素材。

sentences.en: If you ask them to, they've just learned that talking about psychological material is something that you do off the clock.
sentences.zh: 如果你要求他们这样做，他们只是学会了谈论心理学素材是下班后的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, there were times when I was on, you know, another, um, part of the hospital,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有时当我在，你知道，医院的另一个，嗯，部门时，

sentences.en: I would bring this stuff up when we were deciding on how to intervene and what to do in intervention, pick a mechanism of action.
sentences.zh: 当我决定如何干预以及在干预中做什么、选择什么作用机制时，我会提出这些东西。

sentences.en: And the psychiatrist would say, that's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 精神科医生会说：那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: We don't need to talk about it now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在不需要讨论它。

sentences.en: I'll talk to you about it later.
sentences.zh: 我稍后再和你谈。

sentences.en: I, I've got some interesting ideas.
sentences.zh: 我，我有一些有趣的想法。

sentences.en: I'm like, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 我说：你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Like we're literally deciding anyway, that's how they work.
sentences.zh: 我们明明正在做决定，总之，这就是他们的工作方式。

sentences.en: Um, in private conversations, that's what a lot of the psychiatrists that Tanya Lerman documented, that's where they're putting this material.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在私下交谈中，这就是Tanya Lerman记录的许多精神科医生所做的，这就是他们安放这些素材的地方。

sentences.en: And it was also in sort of the cracks of practice.
sentences.zh: 它也存在于实践的缝隙中。

sentences.en: Um, you know, like around the medication prescription, they would keep a patient that they liked longer and they would engage them in these conversations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，比如在开药的时候，他们会把喜欢的患者留得久一点，并与他们进行这些对话。

sentences.en: But like, this is just sort of something that's interesting, not something that's useful.
sentences.zh: 但就像，这只是某种有趣的事情，而不是有用的事情。

sentences.en: And she sort of saw that as maybe that is the part that's useful.
sentences.zh: 而她认为这部分可能才是真正有用的。

sentences.en: So, you know, the official practice had become biological in the nineties.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，官方实践在90年代已经变成了生物学导向。

sentences.en: Um, we're going to finish the human genome project and that's going to tell us how these medications work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们要完成人类基因组计划，那将告诉我们这些药物是如何起作用的。

sentences.en: And then we'll understand why we've been moving in the right direction before we had a reason to.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就会明白，为什么我们在找到理由之前就已经朝着正确的方向前进了。

sentences.en: So the unofficial practice, the private practice of paying attention to the actual human being in front of you had been pushed out of the formal structure of the work.
sentences.zh: 所以非官方的实践，即关注面前真实的人的私人实践，已经被挤出了工作的正式结构。

sentences.en: And so notice what is actually being selected for in a passive process.
sentences.zh: 所以请注意，在一个被动的过程中，到底什么被筛选出来了。

sentences.en: The residents who are passive incentive, passive motivations, the resident who succeeded in this training,
sentences.zh: 那些被动激励、被动动机的住院医师，那些在培训中成功的住院医师，

sentences.en: they're not a resident who are the best at integrating biological and psychological thinking.
sentences.zh: 并不是最擅长整合生物学和心理学思维的住院医师。

sentences.en: The resident who succeeded are the residents who can tolerate the abandonment of the psychological dimension.
sentences.zh: 成功的住院医师是那些能够容忍抛弃心理维度的人。

sentences.en: If you're aware of the psychological dimension at all,
sentences.zh: 如果你完全意识到心理维度的存在，

sentences.en: it's a hindrance to you because it's just dead weight that you're carrying around and thinking about that is not contributing to the process of what we do here.
sentences.zh: 它对你来说就是一种阻碍，因为那只是你随身携带的死重，思考它对我们在这里所做的工作过程毫无贡献。

sentences.en: It's like the guy who's always trying to talk about, you know, Chaucer at the work mill, you know, shut up and make the widgets.
sentences.zh: 就像那个在工厂里总是试图谈论乔叟的人，你知道，闭嘴，好好做零件吧。

sentences.en: Um, the person who knows the thing that, you know, um, that knowledge is actually hurting you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那个知道这件事的人，你知道，嗯，那种知识实际上是在伤害你。

sentences.en: You know, when I graduated in the middle of a recession with a comparative religion degree, I would be like, please for $7 an hour, can I put books on the shelf?
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我毕业时正值经济衰退，拿着比较宗教学位，我会说：请给我每小时7美元，我可以把书放在架子上吗？

sentences.en: And they would be like, oh, you're overqualified.
sentences.zh: 他们会说：哦，你学历过高了。

sentences.en: It's just like, you know, literally you're telling you, we don't really want people, um, with these kinds of degrees or any degree to work here.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，你知道，字面上在告诉你，我们真的不想要拥有这些学位或任何学位的人在这里工作。

sentences.en: You know, the selection pressure is not for skill.
sentences.zh: 你知道，筛选压力不是为了技能。

sentences.en: The selection pressure is for the capacity to be untroubled by the loss of the dimension of the work that requires tolerance for mystery.
sentences.zh: 筛选压力是为了那种能够对失去需要容忍神秘感的工作维度而感到心安理得的能力。

sentences.en: And the residents who cannot make this conversion either leave psychiatry or they develop the chronic professional unhappiness that I see in mid-career psychiatrists when I talk to them and sometimes when they listen to the show.
sentences.zh: 而那些无法完成这种转变的住院医师要么离开精神病学，要么发展出我在与职业中期的精神科医生交谈时，有时在他们听节目时所看到的慢性职业不快乐。

sentences.en: Thank y'all.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: You know, the apparatus does not just capture clinicians.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这套机制不仅仅是俘获了临床医生。

sentences.en: It selects across the entire training pipeline for people whose discomfort with mystery is high enough that they will be relieved when it is taken away from them.
sentences.zh: 它在整个培训管道中筛选出那些对神秘感的不适感足够高的人，以至于当这种神秘感被剥夺时，他们会感到如释重负。

sentences.en: You know, the people who entered psychiatry because they were drawn to the mystery either get washed out or get demoted into private practice, uh, where they don't make anything,
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些因为被神秘感吸引而进入精神病学的人，要么被淘汰，要么被降级到私人诊所，嗯，在那里他们做不出什么名堂，

sentences.en: uh, where they learned to perform the procedural identity while keeping the actual work hidden, which I think there's a pretty big school of.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在那里他们学会了表演这种程序化的身份，同时将实际的工作隐藏起来，我认为这有一个相当大的流派。

sentences.en: Um, it's why I, I, I'm not just,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是为什么我，我，我不仅仅是，

sentences.en: I don't think that we're in 1984 of psychology and that no one out there hears this stuff because a lot of people keep the good work hidden or private.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们处于心理学的“1984”时代，外面没人听到这些东西，因为很多人把好的工作隐藏起来或私下进行。

sentences.en: Um, we're on the side, you know, at the bar and the credentialed psychiatric workforce is by construction,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在旁边，你知道，在酒吧里，而拥有资质的精神科劳动力，从结构上讲，

sentences.en: a workforce whose tolerance for the mystery of psychology has been systematically lowered across years of training.
sentences.zh: 是一支在多年培训中对心理学神秘感的容忍度被系统性降低的劳动力。

sentences.en: And that's not an accident.
sentences.zh: 这不是偶然的。

sentences.en: You know, this is what the apparatus is for.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是这套机制的目的。

sentences.en: And here's one thing I want you to continue to notice in these stories, because a lot of these are just stories.
sentences.zh: 这是我想让你们在这些故事中继续注意的一件事，因为其中很多只是故事。

sentences.en: You know, it's the central observation that the capture that is happening now today, this year,
sentences.zh: 你知道，核心观察是，现在正在发生的俘获，今天，今年，

sentences.en: every psychiatric residency in America is doing it while we're listening to this in America,
sentences.zh: 在美国，每一家精神科住院医师培训项目都在这样做，当我们听这个节目时，

sentences.en: they're processing for a cohort of residents through the same pipeline that Lerman documented 25 years ago, except it's different.
sentences.zh: 他们正在通过Lerman在25年前记录的同一条管道处理一批住院医师，只是现在不同了。

sentences.en: Now, the incentive has not changed, but it's faster.
sentences.zh: 现在，激励机制没有变，但速度更快了。

sentences.en: And the expectation that we even entertain these things is less, you know, if anything, the mechanism has intensified because the pressure to manage caseloads,
sentences.zh: 而且我们甚至去考虑这些事情的期望更低了，你知道，如果有的话，这种机制已经加剧了，因为管理病例的压力，

sentences.en: the medication has only grown, which doesn't mean that it's not needed.
sentences.zh: 药物治疗的需求只会增长，这并不意味着它不需要。

sentences.en: But the biographical inquiry has just shrunk, and the cultural authority of any kind of depth has waned.
sentences.zh: 但个人经历的探究已经萎缩，任何形式的深度的文化权威已经减弱。

sentences.en: And young doctors who entered residency this past summer, you know, 25, hoping to become integrative thinkers about human suffering, are right now being trained out of that hope.
sentences.zh: 而去年夏天进入住院医师培训的年轻医生，你知道，25岁，希望成为人类苦难的综合思考者，现在正被训练得失去这种希望。

sentences.en: And by the time they finish in 29, most of them will have been formed into the kind of doctor the apparatus needs, regardless of what their capacity was to be excellent,
sentences.zh: 到29年他们完成培训时，他们中的大多数人将被塑造成这套机制所需要的医生，无论他们原本有多大的潜力去变得卓越，

sentences.en: or what they wanted when they started, or what they notice, you know, against that system.
sentences.zh: 或者他们开始时想要什么，或者他们注意到了什么，你知道，去对抗那个系统。

sentences.en: Like the guy who's saying, yeah, we know this works, but we are not allowed to know it.
sentences.zh: 就像那个说“是的，我们知道这有效，但我们不被允许知道它”的人。

sentences.en: And I'm like, what?
sentences.zh: 我说：什么？

sentences.en: And he was mad that I pointed out what he said, you know, the same, but he was right that it worked.
sentences.zh: 他对我指出他所说的话感到愤怒，你知道，同样的情况，但他确实是对的，它确实有效。

sentences.en: And that's why he was allowing it to happen as the top guy, you know, or one of the top people.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么作为顶层人物，你知道，或者顶层人物之一，他允许这种情况发生。

sentences.en: The same thing happens with local variations across the other mental health training pipelines.
sentences.zh: 其他心理健康培训管道中也存在类似的局部差异。

sentences.en: You know, master's level social workers, they, these programs, they don't produce social workers who can think across all these layers that I described in that episode.
sentences.zh: 你知道，硕士水平的社会工作者，他们，这些项目，他们培养出的社会工作者无法跨越我在那一集中描述的所有层面进行思考。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: they produce social workers who can complete a DSM-based assessment and write a treatment plan that meets the insurance company's documentation requirements while still being afraid that they didn't do it right.
sentences.zh: 他们培养出的社会工作者能够完成基于DSM的评估，并编写符合保险公司文档要求的治疗计划，同时仍然担心自己做得不对。

sentences.en: Because of the reverence and complexity, the reverence for the complexity, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为对复杂性的敬畏，对复杂性的敬畏，你知道，

sentences.en: master's level counseling programs don't produce counselors who can hold a patient's symbolic life and somatic state at once.
sentences.zh: 硕士水平的咨询项目培养出的咨询师无法同时把握患者的象征性生活和躯体状态。

sentences.en: They produce counselors who have memorized the names of evidence-based protocols and can administer them with, I guess, a lack of insecurity, mechanistic, a mechanistic competence.
sentences.zh: 他们培养出的咨询师背诵了循证协议的名称，并能以一种，我想，缺乏不安全感、机械化的能力来执行它们。

sentences.en: You know, doctoral programs, a lot of times don't produce psychologists who can integrate across schools.
sentences.zh: 你知道，博士项目，很多时候培养出的心理学家无法跨流派整合。

sentences.en: They produce psychologists who can defend a single methodological orientation through a dissertation and then practice within it.
sentences.zh: 他们培养出的心理学家能够通过论文捍卫单一的方法论取向，然后在其中执业。

sentences.en: A lot of those guys are really proud that theirs is the best and the others are bad,
sentences.zh: 那些人中有很多非常自豪，认为自己的是最好的，而其他的是糟糕的，

sentences.en: which cuts you off from a whole lot of knowledge about what those other fields contain in the Venn diagram between what you do and what they do.
sentences.zh: 这让你与关于其他领域在你的工作和他们工作之间的维恩图中包含的知识隔绝开来。

sentences.en: Even if they're wrong, you know, one of the authors that I like a lot, he said, I learned way more from reading bad books because I knew immediately what the lesson was.
sentences.zh: 即使他们错了，你知道，我非常喜欢的一位作者说：我从阅读糟糕的书中学到的东西远多于好书，因为我立刻就知道教训是什么。

sentences.en: When I read a good book, I didn't always know what the lesson was.
sentences.zh: 当我读一本好书时，我并不总是知道教训是什么。

sentences.en: When I read a bad book and I was like, that sucked because of this reason, I knew a new thing not to do.
sentences.zh: 当我读一本糟糕的书时，我会说：因为这个原因，它很烂，我就知道了一个新的不该做的事情。

sentences.en: And then I figured out how to solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 然后我就想出了如何解决这个问题。

sentences.en: When I read a great book, sometimes I was like, that's a fantastic book.
sentences.zh: 每当我读到一本好书时，有时我会想，这真是一本了不起的书。

sentences.en: And I don't really think that I can write like that.
sentences.zh: 而且我真的不认为自己能写出那样的作品。

sentences.en: And that project is finished.
sentences.zh: 那个项目也就此结束了。

sentences.en: When you find something wrong with something, a lot of times that points you to this self-evident,
sentences.zh: 当你发现某件事不对劲时，很多时候这会指向你内心一个不言自明的事实，

sentences.en: self-evident thing in you that is saying the world should be different in a way that you notice and you can do.
sentences.zh: 一个在你内心深处不言自明的东西，它在告诉你，世界本该以某种你所察觉并能有所作为的方式变得不同。

sentences.en: And so that's why I think the history of psychology and all of its weirdness is a lot of fun and also a lot of important lessons.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为心理学的历史及其所有的怪异之处，既充满乐趣，也蕴含着许多重要的教训。

sentences.en: You know, training programs aren't filled with bad people and the training programs are filled, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，培训项目里并非全是坏人，培训项目里，你知道，

sentences.en: largely with people who themselves have been formed by previous iterations of the same pipeline.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上充斥着那些本身就是由同一套流程的先前版本所塑造出来的人。

sentences.en: And the faculty teach what they were taught, the supervisors supervise the way they were supervised,
sentences.zh: 教员们教授的是他们曾经被教导的内容，督导们采用的是他们曾经被督导的方式，

sentences.en: and the whole machine reproduces itself through the slow generational transmission of what kinds of explanations get rewarded.
sentences.zh: 整个机器通过对何种解释能获得认可的缓慢代际传递，不断地自我复制。

sentences.en: And the accountability for the outcome, for whether the clinicians, you know, produced by this pipeline can actually do work anywhere, is nowhere.
sentences.zh: 而对于结果的问责，即这套流程培养出的临床医生是否真的能在任何地方开展工作，却完全处于真空状态。

sentences.en: The schools don't have it.
sentences.zh: 学校没有问责机制。

sentences.en: The boards don't have it.
sentences.zh: 委员会没有问责机制。

sentences.en: The accreditation bodies don't have it.
sentences.zh: 认证机构没有问责机制。

sentences.en: The clinicians, once they are out, have all of it.
sentences.zh: 临床医生一旦出师，就得独自承担这一切。

sentences.en: And the patients become less aware of what's missing because it's less common and they don't know what psychology is supposed to do that they don't have.
sentences.zh: 而患者变得越来越不清楚缺失了什么，因为这种情况越来越普遍，他们也不知道心理学本该提供什么而他们却没有得到。

sentences.en: You know, take Aaron Beck, the founder of CBT.
sentences.zh: 你知道，以认知行为疗法（CBT）的创始人亚伦·贝克为例。

sentences.en: You know, he's trained as a Freudian psychoanalyst at the University of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他在宾夕法尼亚大学接受的是弗洛伊德派精神分析的训练。

sentences.en: He came out of that training the way that a lot of the best critics of any tradition come out, which is, you know,
sentences.zh: 他从那种训练中走出来时，就像任何传统中最优秀的批评者一样，也就是，你知道，

sentences.en: he is this true believer who took the tradition seriously enough to actually test all of its claiMs.
sentences.zh: 他是一位真正的信徒，他足够认真地对待这一传统，以至于真的去检验了它所有的主张。

sentences.en: And he was, by every account from people who knew him, a careful and curious researcher, not a rebel, and not somebody who came in with some axe to grind.
sentences.zh: 据所有认识他的人说，他是一位严谨且充满好奇心的研究者，不是反叛者，也不是那种带着某种不可告人目的而来的人。

sentences.en: He was, you know, the kind of clinician who wanted to know whether the model he had been trained in was actually right.
sentences.zh: 他，你知道，是那种想知道自己所受的训练模型是否真的正确的临床医生。

sentences.en: He was curious and scientific.
sentences.zh: 他既好奇又讲究科学。

sentences.en: So in the, you know, 50s and I think into the early 60s even, you know, Beck runs a series of studies on himself, you know, on these dreams of depressed patients.
sentences.zh: 所以，在50年代，我想甚至到60年代初，你知道，贝克对自己进行了一系列研究，你知道，针对抑郁症患者的这些梦境。

sentences.en: He expected, you know, the studies to validate the classical Freudian hypothesis, which is, you know,
sentences.zh: 他原本预期，你知道，这些研究会验证经典的弗洛伊德假说，也就是，你知道，

sentences.en: depression is anger turned inward against the self and the dreams of depressed patients should therefore contain masochistic content, you know, evidence of self punishment,
sentences.zh: 抑郁症是转向内心的针对自我的愤怒，因此抑郁症患者的梦境应该包含受虐内容，你知道，自我惩罚的证据，

sentences.en: the libidinal mechanisms of aggression and are being redirected at the ego.
sentences.zh: 攻击性的力比多机制被重新导向了自我。

sentences.en: And these were case studies that had built American psychoanalysis, but they were case studies.
sentences.zh: 这些是构建了美国精神分析学的案例研究，但它们终究只是案例研究。

sentences.en: They were things Freud said he found self-evident, not things that data was supporting.
sentences.zh: 它们是弗洛伊德声称自己发现的不言自明的事物，而不是数据所支持的事物。

sentences.en: And so they thought that there would be this masochistic content in the dream and interpret it, you know, back to the patient and watch depression lift.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为梦中会有这种受虐内容，并将其解释给患者听，然后观察抑郁症是否会减轻。

sentences.en: But the studies didn't show that, you know, dream after dream Beck actually found that, um, the content and depressed patients dreams was about, I mean, I guess, depression, loss,
sentences.zh: 但研究并没有显示出这一点，你知道，梦境一个接一个，贝克实际上发现，嗯，抑郁症患者梦境的内容是关于，我是说，我想是关于抑郁、失落、

sentences.en: uh, defeat, deprivation, rejection, uh, hopelessness.
sentences.zh: 呃，挫败、匮乏、拒绝，呃，绝望。

sentences.en: It wasn't what Freud said would be there, which was, you know, anger and rage about, you know, killing the self through some kind of psychosexual lens.
sentences.zh: 那并不是弗洛伊德所说的会存在的内容，也就是，你知道，通过某种性心理视角来杀害自我的愤怒和狂暴。

sentences.en: And so the depressed patient and, you know, Beck's samples were not unconsciously punishing themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以抑郁症患者，你知道，贝克的样本并没有在潜意识里惩罚自己。

sentences.en: They were experiencing reality as a series of losses and their unconscious was processing the losses, not orchestrating some kind of self attack.
sentences.zh: 他们是将现实体验为一系列的失落，而他们的潜意识是在处理这些失落，而不是在策划某种自我攻击。

sentences.en: And so, uh, you know, this is the moment where Beck did something important.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，你知道，这就是贝克做出重要贡献的时刻。

sentences.en: He let the data change his mind and he did not bend the data back into the existing framework.
sentences.zh: 他让数据改变了自己的想法，并没有强行将数据扭曲回现有的框架中。

sentences.en: He did not torture the interpretive, you know, lens to preserve his theory.
sentences.zh: 他没有为了维护自己的理论而扭曲解释的视角。

sentences.en: He'd looked at what was actually happening and said, okay, the patients were processing a view of reality that has been bent in particular ways towards this negative self image.
sentences.zh: 他审视了实际发生的情况，并说，好吧，患者们正在处理一种现实观，这种现实观在某种程度上被扭曲成了这种负面的自我形象。

sentences.en: And the bending happens, you know, in thoughts.
sentences.zh: 而这种扭曲发生在，你知道，思想之中。

sentences.en: So maybe thoughts lead to feelings and feelings lead to behaviors and we can change thoughts and change the system.
sentences.zh: 所以也许思想导致感受，感受导致行为，我们可以改变思想，从而改变整个系统。

sentences.en: So cognitive therapy is born by just sort of bypassing all of Freudian's interpretation.
sentences.zh: 于是认知疗法诞生了，它绕过了所有弗洛伊德式的解释。

sentences.en: Um, I mean, which I think he rejected them because they're largely wrong.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，我认为他拒绝这些解释是因为它们大体上是错误的。

sentences.en: Um, psychoanalysis doesn't really make a ton of sense until it goes to, um, some of the women and some of the developmental psychology experts, you know, Karen Horn, I,
sentences.zh: 嗯，精神分析学在引入一些女性专家和一些发展心理学专家之前，并没有太大的意义，你知道，卡伦·霍妮，我，

sentences.en: I think is in Winnicott are huge.
sentences.zh: 我想温尼科特也是非常重要的。

sentences.en: Um, and then it maybe makes a little bit less sense when it gets picked up by, uh, French theorists.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后当它被法国理论家接手时，可能就更没意义了。

sentences.en: Uh, I don't know what happens to it under Lacan, but so anyway, um, you know, he sees this bloated and indefinitely expensive Beck, not Lacan, um, process.
sentences.zh: 呃，我不知道在拉康的影响下它变成了什么样，但总之，嗯，你知道，他看到了这个臃肿且无限昂贵的贝克（不是拉康），嗯，过程。

sentences.en: That's full of people who thought they were God and they had this massive insecurity and they're, you know, sort of playing God with patients' lives.
sentences.zh: 里面充满了自以为是上帝的人，他们有着巨大的不安全感，你知道，在某种程度上把患者的生命当作儿戏。

sentences.en: They're paying, you know, being the ultimate authority on the patient's own, you know, subjective self.
sentences.zh: 他们表现得，你知道，是患者自身主观自我的终极权威。

sentences.en: And, and,
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，

sentences.en: and some of them have these massive insecurity complexes and they're narcissists and they sit in chairs and analyze people and tell them what's wrong with them using these metaphors that are treated as scientific fact.
sentences.zh: 而且他们中的一些人有巨大的不安全感综合症，他们是自恋者，他们坐在椅子上分析别人，用那些被当作科学事实的隐喻来告诉别人他们有什么问题。

sentences.en: And Beck starts to realize that they're not scientific fact.
sentences.zh: 而贝克开始意识到这些并不是科学事实。

sentences.en: They're not really even supported by the science.
sentences.zh: 它们甚至没有得到科学的真正支持。

sentences.en: You know, the Rosenhan investigation that you talked about, you know, Rosenhan checking himself and graduate school students into a hospital.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你提到的罗森汉恩调查，你知道，罗森汉恩把自己和研究生送进医院。

sentences.en: Um, you know, he, he sees this crisis of confidence coming and Beck saw the problem before Rosenhan did, you know, his answer was clinical, not satirical.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，他，他看到了即将到来的信任危机，而贝克在罗森汉恩之前就看到了这个问题，你知道，他的回答是临床性的，而不是讽刺性的。

sentences.en: Um, he was actually trying to fix it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他实际上是在试图解决它。

sentences.en: Whereas Rosenhan was kind of trying to actively blow it up.
sentences.zh: 而罗森汉恩则是在试图积极地摧毁它。

sentences.en: And when you do that, all you do is make an insecure.
sentences.zh: 当你这样做时，你所做的只是制造了一种不安全感。

sentences.en: So when you make it system that acts badly, when it's insecure, um, and that insecurity comes from numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以当你制造了一个表现糟糕的系统，当它感到不安全时，嗯，而这种不安全感源于数字。

sentences.en: Thank you, theater reporter.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，戏剧记者。

sentences.en: When you make that system more insecure, all you're going to do is make it act more badly or, or act badly more.
sentences.zh: 当你让那个系统变得更加不安全时，你所做的只会让它表现得更糟，或者，或者更频繁地表现糟糕。

sentences.en: Um, it's kind of like in therapy when someone's ashamed and they think the shame is going to motivate them to do better, but they're doing terribly and they're full of shame.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有点像在治疗中，当某人感到羞耻，他们认为羞耻会激励他们做得更好，但他们表现得很糟糕，而且充满了羞耻感。

sentences.en: The shame is not the answer and shaming them more does not motivate them to change.
sentences.zh: 羞耻并不是答案，羞辱他们并不能激励他们改变。

sentences.en: That's why I think the resistance to this thing has to be passive.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为对这件事的抵制必须是消极的。

sentences.en: Um, any active resistance is just going to be co-opted Eden and probably some of the people involved punish, you know, involved in trying to make the system feel bad.
sentences.zh: 嗯，任何积极的抵制都只会被伊甸园（Eden）和一些参与其中的人所利用，他们试图让系统感到难受。

sentences.en: You know, just the thought, you know, as the patient reports it in this moment, let's ask whether or not it's true.
sentences.zh: 你知道，仅仅是那个想法，你知道，正如患者在这一刻所报告的那样，让我们问问它是否属实。

sentences.en: You know, Beck says, this is, that's an easier thing to do than all of psychoanalysis is just say, the thing that you're thinking, is it supported by evidence?
sentences.zh: 你知道，贝克说，这比整个精神分析学更容易做到，就是说，你正在想的事情，它有证据支持吗？

sentences.en: And then you teach them that that thought is not always them.
sentences.zh: 然后你教他们，那个想法并不总是代表他们自己。

sentences.en: That if they can say, yeah, well, it's not true, or it couldn't really be that way.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能说，是的，嗯，那不是真的，或者事情不可能是那样的。

sentences.en: Then you say, okay, you're having this thought, but the thought is not having you.
sentences.zh: 那么你就说，好吧，你有这个想法，但不是这个想法控制了你。

sentences.en: You don't always have to have this thought.
sentences.zh: 你不必总是持有这个想法。

sentences.en: Is there another thought we can have?
sentences.zh: 我们能有别的想法吗？

sentences.en: And that sounds stupid, but for the time, I mean, it's pretty revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很愚蠢，但在当时，我是说，这相当具有革命性。

sentences.en: And this is, by the way, like the same move that, you know, it's a little bit more ornamented now, but like it's the same move that a parts-based therapist makes,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这就像，你知道，现在稍微修饰了一下，但就像基于部分的治疗师所做的动作一样，

sentences.en: that a mindfulness-based therapist is doing.
sentences.zh: 正念治疗师正在做的事情。

sentences.en: A new modality worth doing is it's dealing with multiplicity in this way where you separate the person from the thought they're having in that moment.
sentences.zh: 一种值得尝试的新模式，它以这种方式处理多样性，即你将人与他们在那一刻产生的想法分离开来。

sentences.en: And that separation is clinically powerful.
sentences.zh: 而这种分离在临床上是强有力的。

sentences.en: It's the beginning of a process because if you, but I think if you stop there, you know,
sentences.zh: 这是一个过程的开始，因为如果你，但我认为如果你停在那里，你知道，

sentences.en: if you're just only doing the pointing out where their beliefs are not supported by evidence, like some people criticize that CBT is, does too often,
sentences.zh: 如果你只是指出他们的信念没有证据支持，就像有些人批评CBT经常做的那样，

sentences.en: even though it says it does other things.
sentences.zh: 尽管它声称自己也做其他事情。

sentences.en: I think stopping there is bad because that's a very surface level way to do therapy.
sentences.zh: 我认为停在那里是不好的，因为那是一种非常表层的治疗方式。

sentences.en: And the person does not have the tools at that point to continue to heal themselves outside of the room.
sentences.zh: 而且在那一点上，当事人并没有工具在咨询室外继续治愈自己。

sentences.en: Um, so, uh, which is another thing that we don't look for in research.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，呃，这也是我们在研究中没有寻找的东西。

sentences.en: Did this person learn something that allowed them to not ever come back to therapy, to solve the next problem, to grow, to be reconnected to a process of growth?
sentences.zh: 这个人是否学到了什么，使他们能够不再回到治疗中，去解决下一个问题，去成长，去重新连接到成长的过程中？

sentences.en: How do you do a randomized, double blind, you know, randomized control trial for that?
sentences.zh: 你如何为那个做随机、双盲、你知道，随机对照试验？

sentences.en: But I think that's what good therapy does.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这就是好的治疗所做的事情。

sentences.en: And my critique of CBT, when you just stop at the process I just described is that you haven't done that yet.
sentences.zh: 我对CBT的批评是，当你仅仅停留在刚才描述的过程中时，你还没有做到这一点。

sentences.en: So, you know, this is what Beck stumbles on so far.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这就是贝克目前所发现的。

sentences.en: So good story of a curious clinician who lets his data change his mind.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于好奇的临床医生让数据改变自己想法的好故事。

sentences.en: And then he builds a useful intervention out of what he learned.
sentences.zh: 然后他根据所学到的东西建立了一个有用的干预措施。

sentences.en: And this is how science is supposed to work.
sentences.zh: 这就是科学应该运作的方式。

sentences.en: But here's what happens next.
sentences.zh: 但接下来发生的事情是这样的。

sentences.en: This is where the apparatus sees what Beck did and turns him into something that he never intended to be.
sentences.zh: 这就是机构看到贝克所做的事情，并把他变成了他从未打算成为的样子。

sentences.en: Never said he was.
sentences.zh: 他从未说过他是那样的人。

sentences.en: There were three properties of what Beck had built that made it perfect.
sentences.zh: 贝克所建立的东西有三个属性，使它变得完美。

sentences.en: Perfect for the establishment.
sentences.zh: 对体制来说非常完美。

sentences.en: The cognitive model was manualizable.
sentences.zh: 认知模型是可以手册化的。

sentences.en: You could write the steps down and a different clinician could follow them.
sentences.zh: 你可以写下步骤，不同的临床医生可以遵循它们。

sentences.en: It was a technique more than an interpretive lens.
sentences.zh: 它更多是一种技术，而不是一种解释的视角。

sentences.en: So the cognitive model was time limited.
sentences.zh: 所以认知模型是有时间限制的。

sentences.en: Beck's original protocols ran on 12 to 16 sessions, which fit insurance coverage, you know,
sentences.zh: 贝克最初的方案运行在12到16次会话，这完美地符合保险覆盖，你知道，

sentences.en: periods perfectly because that's how long his interventions were designed to be implemented and they were formulizable.
sentences.zh: 周期，因为这就是他的干预措施被设计实施的时间长度，而且它们是可以公式化的。

sentences.en: So they were, they followed a formula.
sentences.zh: 所以它们，它们遵循一个公式。

sentences.en: You didn't really have a lot of leeway in that formula.
sentences.zh: 你在那个公式中并没有太多的余地。

sentences.en: So you could say how long the whole process would take, which had never happened before.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说整个过程需要多长时间，这在以前从未发生过。

sentences.en: Psychoanalysis, you just talked until you all of a sudden stumbled on some kind of insight and then hopefully the insight changed something.
sentences.zh: 精神分析学，你只是不停地谈话，直到你突然偶然发现某种洞察力，然后希望洞察力能改变什么。

sentences.en: But usually it didn't.
sentences.zh: 但通常它并没有。

sentences.en: And so the cognitive model was measurable.
sentences.zh: 所以认知模型是可衡量的。

sentences.en: And the Beck depression inventory, which Beck himself developed in 1961, now, you know, gave you this number.
sentences.zh: 而贝克抑郁量表，贝克本人在1961年开发的，现在，你知道，给了你这个数字。

sentences.en: The number went up or down.
sentences.zh: 数字上升或下降。

sentences.en: You could see in real time whether or not you were doing anything that produced a change and whether you were just talking to somebody who was entertaining you while their depression actually got worse because you're measuring it the whole time.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时看到你是否在做任何产生改变的事情，以及你是否只是在和一个逗你开心的人交谈，而他们的抑郁症实际上却加重了，因为你一直在测量它。

sentences.en: You're not just, you know, shooting from the hip about if they're depressed or not in session.
sentences.zh: 你不仅仅是，你知道，在会话中凭空猜测他们是否抑郁。

sentences.en: And those three properties, manualizable plus time-limited plus measurable, are the properties that the emerging managed care apparatus needed.
sentences.zh: 而这三个属性，可手册化加有时限加可衡量，正是新兴的管理式医疗机构所需要的属性。

sentences.en: And the managed care apparatus needed a therapy that it could buy in bulk, deliver to interchangeable patients, time cap, and then audit.
sentences.zh: 管理式医疗机构需要一种可以批量购买、提供给可互换的患者、有时限限制，然后进行审计的疗法。

sentences.en: And Beck, completely by accident, working in good faith on a real clinical problem,
sentences.zh: 而贝克，完全是偶然的，在真诚地处理一个真正的临床问题时，

sentences.en: had produced the only major therapy framework in American psychiatry that satisfied all three requirements at once.
sentences.zh: 在美国精神病学中产生了一个同时满足这三个要求的唯一主要治疗框架。

sentences.en: And the apparatus did not just select CBT because CBT was the most effective therapy.
sentences.zh: 而该机构选择CBT不仅仅是因为CBT是最有效的疗法。

sentences.en: It did that later.
sentences.zh: 那是后来才发生的。

sentences.en: The apparatus selected CBT because CBT was the therapy whose form most successfully removed the mystery from the work.
sentences.zh: 该机构选择CBT是因为CBT是那种其形式最成功地消除了工作神秘感的疗法。

sentences.en: And the cognitive content can be specified.
sentences.zh: 而且认知内容是可以指定的。

sentences.en: Beck thought all that stuff was still there.
sentences.zh: 贝克认为所有那些东西仍然存在。

sentences.en: He didn't strip it out.
sentences.zh: 他并没有把它剥离出来。

sentences.en: He thought Freud was wrong about this one thing, but he wasn't really trying to kill the depths.
sentences.zh: 他认为弗洛伊德在这一件事上错了，但他并不是真的想扼杀深度。

sentences.en: He just got used, you know, by the apparatus to kill the depths.
sentences.zh: 他只是被，你知道，被机构利用来扼杀深度。

sentences.en: And the homework assignments in CBT, they can be enumerated.
sentences.zh: 而CBT中的家庭作业，它们是可以列举的。

sentences.en: The thought record can be reviewed by a supervisor who's not in the room.
sentences.zh: 思维记录可以由不在房间里的督导审查。

sentences.en: The treatment can be evaluated by reading the documentation.
sentences.zh: 治疗可以通过阅读文档来评估。

sentences.en: There was finally something other than taking the therapist's word for it, which, you know, people were angry because they increasingly, more so after Beck,
sentences.zh: 终于有了除了听信治疗师的话之外的东西，你知道，人们很生气，因为他们越来越多地，在贝克之后更是如此，

sentences.en: had done this too much with Freud.
sentences.zh: 在弗洛伊德身上做得太多了。

sentences.en: How do we let people in and find out if you're full of shit?
sentences.zh: 我们如何让人们进来并找出你是否在胡说八道？

sentences.en: Well, CBT gives you a lot of numbers that let you do that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，CBT给了你很多数字，让你能做到这一点。

sentences.en: And so everything that makes CBT manualizable and measurable is also what makes CBT the kind of therapy that can be practiced without entering the mystery.
sentences.zh: 所以使CBT可手册化和可衡量的一切，也是使CBT成为那种可以在不进入神秘领域的情况下进行实践的疗法的原因。

sentences.en: A skilled therapist doing the deep work is doing something that the manual cannot describe, and they know it,
sentences.zh: 一个做深层工作的熟练治疗师正在做一些手册无法描述的事情，他们知道这一点，

sentences.en: and they protect that work from the manual by holding it in their own clinical mind while producing the documentation that the apparatus requires.
sentences.zh: 他们通过将这项工作保持在自己的临床头脑中，同时制作机构要求的文档，来保护这项工作免受手册的干扰。

sentences.en: But the unskilled CBT therapist, the procedural worker, you know, the apparatus actually wants you more.
sentences.zh: 但那个不熟练的CBT治疗师，那个程序化工作者，你知道，机构实际上更想要你。

sentences.en: Because just like the psychiatrist that we talked about, you know, Tanya Lerman, if you are trying to juggle things other than the number, you're not as effective,
sentences.zh: 因为就像我们谈到的精神科医生，你知道，坦尼娅·勒曼，如果你试图处理数字以外的事情，你就不那么有效，

sentences.en: you're not as efficient, and you look less evidence-based.
sentences.zh: 你就不那么高效，而且看起来不那么基于证据。

sentences.en: Why are you taking time to talk to this person?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要花时间跟这个人说话？

sentences.en: You know how many therapy candidates I've had that had a supervisor that said that, and they were like, well, let's talk therapy.
sentences.zh: 你知道我有多少治疗候选人，他们的督导说过那样的话，他们说，好吧，让我们谈谈治疗。

sentences.en: And they're like, no, I mean about stuff other than the therapy.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，我是说关于治疗以外的事情。

sentences.en: Why are you trying to get them to like you?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要试图让他们喜欢你？

sentences.en: And then they, as a rebellion against that, they did this study and said, oh, the evidence shows that if you get rapport with the patient,
sentences.zh: 然后他们，作为对那种情况的反叛，他们做了这项研究并说，哦，证据表明，如果你与患者建立了融洽关系，

sentences.en: which rapport is just like a word for you like them, and they like you, and they enjoy being around you.
sentences.zh: 融洽关系只是一个词，意思是他们喜欢你，你喜欢他们，他们喜欢和你在一起。

sentences.en: It's a fancy word for that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个花哨的词。

sentences.en: Then the intervention will work better.
sentences.zh: 那么干预措施会更有效。

sentences.en: The science supports that now.
sentences.zh: 科学现在支持这一点。

sentences.en: Why did we run that research study?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要进行那项研究？

sentences.en: Why did we, for the industry to have needed to be there, you know, in the 80s, that we ran studies to see if the patient had rapport with the clinician, if therapy went better?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们，为了行业需要，你知道，在80年代，我们进行了研究来看看患者是否与临床医生有融洽关系，治疗是否会更好？

sentences.en: Why is that not just a goal?
sentences.zh: 为什么那不仅仅是一个目标？

sentences.en: Why does it need to be tied to mechanism of action?
sentences.zh: 为什么它需要与作用机制挂钩？

sentences.en: And also, of course it is.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然确实如此。

sentences.en: And so many things, like every angle, that's the dumbest thing in the world.
sentences.zh: 还有很多事情，比如每一个角度，那都是世界上最愚蠢的事情。

sentences.en: But that increasingly is the world that this world became.
sentences.zh: 但这越来越成为这个世界所演变成的样子。

sentences.en: You know, the apparatus can't tell the difference between the good CBT practitioner and the bad CBT practitioner.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这套机制无法区分优秀的CBT（认知行为疗法）从业者和糟糕的CBT从业者。

sentences.en: And so it's why a lot of people, or the good psychiatrist, or the bad psychiatrist, and it's why I think a lot of people defend psychiatry or CBT and say, hey,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么很多人，或者优秀的精神科医生，或者糟糕的精神科医生，这也是为什么我认为很多人为精神病学或CBT辩护，说，嘿，

sentences.en: it's not as bad as everyone says.
sentences.zh: 它并没有大家说的那么糟糕。

sentences.en: And then also why people attack it hyperbolically is because they sort of know that there's good ones out there and bad ones out there, but they can't tell the difference.
sentences.zh: 而人们之所以夸大其词地攻击它，是因为他们隐约知道这里面有好人也有坏人，但他们无法分辨。

sentences.en: But they kind of tell that the bad ones like this more or they thrive in that water.
sentences.zh: 但他们能感觉到坏人更喜欢这种环境，或者说他们在那种水域里如鱼得水。

sentences.en: So, you know, screw the lake.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，去他的那个湖吧。

sentences.en: You know, the apparatus can't tell the difference between those practitioners, but it prefers one.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这套机制无法区分那些从业者，但它偏爱其中一种。

sentences.en: And the apparatus does not want to tell the difference because the difference is the variable to the apparatus has been constructed to deny.
sentences.zh: 而且这套机制不想去区分，因为这种差异正是这套机制被构建出来所要否认的变量。

sentences.en: And so telling the difference would require admitting that something matters, which can't be measured, and admitting that would dissolve the entire institutional structure.
sentences.zh: 所以，要区分它们就需要承认某些无法衡量的事物很重要，而承认这一点会瓦解整个体制结构。

sentences.en: So we can't have this conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不能进行这种对话。

sentences.en: And now Beck himself was, you know, not part of the apparatus.
sentences.zh: 而贝克（Beck）本人，你知道，并不属于这套机制的一部分。

sentences.en: By all accounts, he was, you know, late into his life, a humble guy who was clear.
sentences.zh: 据各方说法，你知道，在他晚年，他是一个谦逊且头脑清醒的人。

sentences.en: CBT is one tool.
sentences.zh: CBT只是一种工具。

sentences.en: And he continued to read other traditions across his career.
sentences.zh: 他在整个职业生涯中持续阅读其他传统理论。

sentences.en: He revised, you know, his later work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他修订了他后期的作品。

sentences.en: He saw it as something that should change, not, you know, a solution to the problem that was American psychology.
sentences.zh: 他将其视为一种应该不断变化的东西，而不是，你知道，美国心理学问题的终极解决方案。

sentences.en: When he developed a recovery-oriented cognitive therapy for serious mental illness in his later years, working with Paul Grant.
sentences.zh: 当他在晚年与保罗·格兰特（Paul Grant）合作，为严重精神疾病开发了以康复为导向的认知疗法时。

sentences.en: And that was much more kind of relational and integrative,
sentences.zh: 那是一种更具关系性和整合性的方法，

sentences.en: much more attuned to the developmental trauma in the context of psychosis than the standard CBT manuals would have allowed.
sentences.zh: 比标准的CBT手册所允许的更能适应精神病背景下的发育性创伤。

sentences.en: But you can't do that now.
sentences.zh: 但你现在做不到这一点了。

sentences.en: I was given a manual to do CBT for schizophrenia and psychosis in the hospital that I read, and it was pretty wild.
sentences.zh: 我在医院里拿到过一本做精神分裂症和精神病CBT的手册，我读了读，那真是相当离谱。

sentences.en: You were just kind of supposed to tell people that we're having delusions, that their delusions were not evidence-based, that they needed to stop.
sentences.zh: 你基本上只是被要求告诉那些有妄想症的人，他们的妄想没有证据支持，他们需要停止这些想法。

sentences.en: That was, I don't know, 10 techniques to do that.
sentences.zh: 那大概是，我不知道，实现这一目标的10种技巧。

sentences.en: We didn't get the Paul Grant model.
sentences.zh: 我们没有得到保罗·格兰特的模型。

sentences.en: It wasn't selected.
sentences.zh: 它没有被选中。

sentences.en: Even though Beck made, like most of these people, some good, some bad, some in the middle, things in his life, the apparatus picks what it wants.
sentences.zh: 尽管贝克像大多数人一样，在他的一生中做过一些好事、坏事，还有一些平庸的事，但机制会挑选它想要的部分。

sentences.en: You know, Beck was in many ways the version of himself that the apparatus did not want.
sentences.zh: 你知道，贝克在许多方面是他自己所不希望成为的那种版本。

sentences.en: You know, the Beck who was integrating, the Beck who was reading the semantic literature, the Beck who was acknowledging the limits of the cognitive frame,
sentences.zh: 你知道，那个在进行整合的贝克，那个在阅读语义学文献的贝克，那个承认认知框架局限性的贝克，

sentences.en: the late Beck especially.
sentences.zh: 尤其是晚年的贝克。

sentences.en: That Beck was not the Beck who got reproduced in the textbooks and in the training prograMs.
sentences.zh: 那个贝克并不是教科书和培训项目中被复制出来的那个贝克。

sentences.en: Not even in the CBT Institute when you get certified in CBT, because you're getting certified in CBT, not certified in Aaron Beck.
sentences.zh: 甚至在CBT协会里当你获得CBT认证时也不是，因为你获得的是CBT认证，而不是亚伦·贝克（Aaron Beck）认证。

sentences.en: And I want to be specific about Beck's relationship to Spitzer and Francis and the DSM project as a character, because this is the part that gets lost in the standard narrative.
sentences.zh: 我想具体谈谈贝克与斯皮策（Spitzer）、弗朗西斯（Francis）以及DSM（精神疾病诊断与统计手册）项目之间的关系，因为这是标准叙事中被遗漏的部分。

sentences.en: Beck did not love what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 贝克并不喜欢他们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: He was not particularly enthusiastic about the DSM-3.
sentences.zh: 他对DSM-3并不是特别热衷。

sentences.en: He had reservations about the categorical model.
sentences.zh: 他对分类模型持有保留意见。

sentences.en: He understood that the depression and anxiety did not, in fact, carve nature at their joints the way that the manual was pretending they did.
sentences.zh: 他明白抑郁症和焦虑症实际上并没有像手册所假装的那样，精准地切中自然的关节。

sentences.en: But Beck was a researcher, and the DSM-3 gave him a research framework.
sentences.zh: 但贝克是一位研究者，而DSM-3为他提供了一个研究框架。

sentences.en: And as his work fit into that framework better than most other work, that framework was what was taken.
sentences.zh: 由于他的工作比大多数其他工作更适合那个框架，所以那个框架被采纳了。

sentences.en: Whether or not he endorsed everything that the framework was doing, it's what was taken from him.
sentences.zh: 无论他是否认可该框架所做的一切，这就是从他身上被拿走的东西。

sentences.en: And it's all of him that survived.
sentences.zh: 这也是他留存下来的全部。

sentences.en: And the apparatus didn't need his endorsement to do it.
sentences.zh: 而且这套机制不需要他的认可就能做到这一点。

sentences.en: It didn't need his tools, like Francis, like Spencer.
sentences.zh: 它不需要他的工具，就像弗朗西斯和斯皮策那样。

sentences.en: You can protest these symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 你可以抗议这些症状。

sentences.en: You can say you were using me wrong.
sentences.zh: 你可以说你用错我了。

sentences.en: You can say I made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 你可以说我犯了个错误。

sentences.en: Like John Nash, you know, we talked about the mathematician who was used to sort of create the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 就像约翰·纳什（John Nash），你知道，我们谈到过那位被用来创造冷战的数学家。

sentences.en: You can say I was crazy, and I was wrong, and it does not matter.
sentences.zh: 你可以说我疯了，我错了，但这无关紧要。

sentences.en: We've taken what we need from you.
sentences.zh: 我们已经从你身上拿走了我们需要的东西。

sentences.en: We have taken you at your most insecure because it flatters us and are most insecure so well that we don't have to see our own insecurity.
sentences.zh: 我们利用了你最不安全感的部分，因为它太讨好我们了，我们自己的不安全感也如此之深，以至于我们不必去正视它。

sentences.en: And the apparatus didn't steal from Beck, and it didn't corrupt it.
sentences.zh: 这套机制没有从贝克那里偷窃，也没有腐蚀他。

sentences.en: It didn't force Beck to do anything he didn't want to do.
sentences.zh: 它没有强迫贝克做任何他不想做的事。

sentences.en: What it did is something subtler and more powerful.
sentences.zh: 它所做的是一种更微妙、更强大的事情。

sentences.en: It took the parts of Beck's work that it needed.
sentences.zh: 它取走了贝克工作中它所需要的部分。

sentences.en: It scaled those parts.
sentences.zh: 它将这些部分规模化。

sentences.en: It let the rest atrophy.
sentences.zh: 它让其余的部分萎缩。

sentences.en: The manualizable parts get manualized.
sentences.zh: 可手册化的部分被手册化了。

sentences.en: The measurable parts get measured.
sentences.zh: 可衡量的部分被衡量了。

sentences.en: The time-limited parts get time-capped.
sentences.zh: 有时限的部分被限制了时间。

sentences.en: And the parts that Beck did not, you know, want to be taken out, the curiosity, the integration, the willingness to revise,
sentences.zh: 而那些贝克不希望被剔除的部分，比如好奇心、整合性、修订的意愿，

sentences.en: the late career humility, the recovery-oriented work with serious mental illness, the acknowledgement of the environment,
sentences.zh: 晚年的谦逊、针对严重精神疾病的康复导向工作、对环境的认可，

sentences.en: the implicit acknowledgement that the cognitive frame was just a starting point and not the destination.
sentences.zh: 以及对认知框架仅仅是一个起点而非终点的隐含承认。

sentences.en: And it should never be mistaken for that.
sentences.zh: 它绝不应该被误认为是终点。

sentences.en: All of that gets quietly left out of the version of CBT that gets reproduced at scale.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都被悄悄地排除在规模化复制的CBT版本之外了。

sentences.en: And the Beck that you encountered in a master's-level training program in 2026 is not Beck.
sentences.zh: 而你在2026年的硕士培训项目中遇到的那个贝克，并不是真正的贝克。

sentences.en: It's the parts of Beck that the apparatus selected for.
sentences.zh: 那是机制所筛选出的贝克的部分。

sentences.en: And it's the Beck as protocol.
sentences.zh: 那是作为协议的贝克。

sentences.en: Beck with the curiosity removed, Beck as something an 18-month online degree can teach, a graduate to do with fidelity.
sentences.zh: 去除了好奇心的贝克，作为18个月在线学位就能教给毕业生的、可以忠实执行的贝克。

sentences.en: And the people who reproduce this version of Beck do not even know that it's not Beck.
sentences.zh: 而那些复制这个版本贝克的人，甚至不知道那不是贝克。

sentences.en: They've not only encountered a captured version.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅接触到了一个被捕获的版本。

sentences.en: They believe that they are doing what Beck did, when they are doing the worst things, and sometimes the things he disagreed with.
sentences.zh: 他们相信自己在做贝克所做的事，而实际上他们正在做最糟糕的事情，有时甚至是贝克所反对的事情。

sentences.en: They're doing what the apparatus expected from what Beck did.
sentences.zh: 他们正在做的是机制所期望的、基于贝克所做之事的结果。

sentences.en: You know, when you take objectivity, when you take quantification to this extreme, you end up back in a very religious place.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你把客观性、量化推向这种极端时，你最终会回到一个非常宗教化的地方。

sentences.en: How many of the founders of the world religions would like the religion as it currently exists, and its majority if they showed back up?
sentences.zh: 如果世界各大宗教的创始人重新出现，他们会喜欢现在存在的宗教及其主流形式吗？

sentences.en: Now, this is what capture looks like.
sentences.zh: 现在，这就是被捕获的样子。

sentences.en: It doesn't require villains.
sentences.zh: 它不需要恶棍。

sentences.en: It requires no conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 它不需要阴谋。

sentences.en: It does not require the founder's consent or refusal.
sentences.zh: 它不需要创始人的同意或拒绝。

sentences.en: It requires only the founder's work, contain properties that the apparatus needs,
sentences.zh: 它只需要创始人的作品包含机制所需要的属性，

sentences.en: and that the apparatus have enough institutional power to scale the useful properties while letting the rest fade.
sentences.zh: 并且机制拥有足够的制度权力来规模化这些有用的属性，同时让其余部分消亡。

sentences.en: You know, Beck was a careful, curious clinician who let his data change his mind.
sentences.zh: 你知道，贝克是一位谨慎、好奇的临床医生，他会让数据改变自己的想法。

sentences.en: The version of Beck that lives in the apparatus is a checkliSt.
sentences.zh: 活在机制里的那个贝克版本是一个检查清单。

sentences.en: And the distance between those two things is the distance that I'm asking you to see, because the same distance shows up in every modality the apparatus has captured.
sentences.zh: 这两者之间的距离就是我要求你们看到的距离，因为同样的距离出现在机制所捕获的每一种模式中。

sentences.en: And the same mechanism produces it every time.
sentences.zh: 而且同样的机制每次都会产生同样的结果。

sentences.en: So, Campbell's law says that any quantitative indicator used to make decisions distorts the process that it is meant to monitor.
sentences.zh: 所以，坎贝尔定律（Campbell's law）说，任何用于决策的定量指标都会扭曲它旨在监测的过程。

sentences.en: And Goodhart's law is the same observation, sort of.
sentences.zh: 古德哈特定律（Goodhart's law）也是同样的观察结果，某种程度上。

sentences.en: You know, when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measurement.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当一个指标变成目标时，它就不再是一个好的指标了。

sentences.en: Because everything that isn't the measurement is now able to be sacrificed.
sentences.zh: 因为所有不是该指标的事物现在都可以被牺牲掉。

sentences.en: Anything that isn't that number or can't be captured in a number is now ruined.
sentences.zh: 任何不是那个数字或无法被数字捕捉的东西现在都被毁了。

sentences.en: And no target, no real target in the real world exists in that way.
sentences.zh: 而在现实世界中，没有任何真正的目标是以那种方式存在的。

sentences.en: Corey Doctro writes about inshittification in technology.
sentences.zh: 科里·多克托罗（Cory Doctorow）写过关于科技领域的“垃圾化”（enshittification）。

sentences.en: You know, he writes about the rot economy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他写的是关于腐烂经济学。

sentences.en: You know, Ed Zetron has a podcast on that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，埃德·泽特隆（Ed Zitron）有一个关于这个的播客。

sentences.en: That's pretty good if you are interested in the economics of LLMs.
sentences.zh: 如果你对大语言模型（LLM）的经济学感兴趣，那还不错。

sentences.en: But, you know, the patterns that they're looking at in Silicon Valley are describing what platforms do when they have eliminated their competition,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他们在硅谷观察到的模式，描述了平台在消除竞争对手后会做什么，

sentences.en: and they capture regulators, and they've locked users in,
sentences.zh: 他们捕获了监管机构，锁定了用户，

sentences.en: and then they make the product systematically worse on purpose to extract more value from people who have nowhere else to go.
sentences.zh: 然后他们系统性地让产品变得更糟，目的是从那些无处可去的人身上榨取更多价值。

sentences.en: And Silicon Valley may hit a monopoly before the other institutions in America do.
sentences.zh: 硅谷可能比美国的其他机构更早达到垄断。

sentences.en: Or they may hit that point of total institutional capture and then freedom that results in monopoly conditions.
sentences.zh: 或者他们可能达到了完全的制度捕获点，然后是导致垄断条件的自由。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that we should let them do that or other things do it, but it may be a good case study in just how power and bureaucracy work.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们应该让他们这样做，或者让其他事物这样做，但这可能是一个关于权力和官僚机构如何运作的很好的案例研究。

sentences.en: You know, the pattern goes like this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，模式是这样的。

sentences.en: First, the platform is good to users to attract them.
sentences.zh: 首先，平台对用户很好以吸引他们。

sentences.en: And then once the users are locked in, the platform is good to the business customers at the expense of the users.
sentences.zh: 然后一旦用户被锁定，平台就会以牺牲用户为代价对商业客户好。

sentences.en: And then once the business customers are also locked in, then the platform extracts value from both,
sentences.zh: 然后一旦商业客户也被锁定，平台就会从双方榨取价值，

sentences.en: making the experience worse for everyone except for the platform's shareholders.
sentences.zh: 让除了平台股东之外的所有人的体验都变得更糟。

sentences.en: And the reason that this is possible is that the platform has eliminated all the forces that would normally discipline a bad actor.
sentences.zh: 之所以可能做到这一点，是因为平台已经消除了所有本应约束不良行为者的力量。

sentences.en: And market competition is gone because the platform has, you know, bought or destroyed its competitors.
sentences.zh: 市场竞争消失了，因为平台已经，你知道，买下或摧毁了它的竞争对手。

sentences.en: And then the regulatory oversight is gone because the platform is large enough to capture the regulators or the regulators become part of the company.
sentences.zh: 监管监督消失了，因为平台足够大，可以捕获监管机构，或者监管机构成为了公司的一部分。

sentences.en: And then vice versa.
sentences.zh: 反之亦然。
